headline: Nepali Congress opens 15th convention as Deuba's invitation is left with his guard
dek: Candidate nominations follow Monday, but party rivals could not hand Sher Bahadur Deuba his own invitation.
body_markdown:
Nepali Congress, Nepal's oldest democratic party, opened its 15th General Convention at Kathmandu's Tundikhel open stage at 2 pm on Sunday, October 4, party spokesperson Devraj Chalise said, according to Nepal Press. Candidate nominations follow on Monday, October 5, with the convention's closing session and remaining programs running through Tuesday, October 6, OnlineKhabar reported.

The event matters beyond party ritual. Whoever wins the top posts this week will speak for the party. Delegates at Tundikhel begin choosing those contenders on Monday, ekantipur.com and Nepalnews.com reported.

The party organizing committee booked hotel rooms across Kathmandu for roughly 10,000 delegates and well-wishers, Khabarhub and Nepalnews.com reported. Eight parking sites went up around the venue for vehicles bringing participants and representatives, Nepal Press reported. Thirty health workers and two ambulances stood on standby, with health checks also run at the hotels, ekantipur.com reported.

## The invitation that did not land

Sher Bahadur Deuba, a former prime minister and former Nepali Congress president, has urged a boycott of the convention, Desh Sanchar reported. He has refused to join the convention his rival Gagan Thapa now leads as party president, the Kathmandu Post reported. Thapa sent co-general secretary Yogendra Chaudhary to Deuba's residence to hand deliver an invitation asking him to attend as chief guest, OnlineKhabar and Nepal Press reported.

Chaudhary said the delegation never reached Deuba himself.

"We did not meet him, we went right inside the house. When we called Bhanuji, we could not reach him either. After that we went to the house, gave it to the security guard and came back," Chaudhary told OnlineKhabar, referring to Deuba's private secretary Bhanu Deuba.

Neither OnlineKhabar nor Nepal Press carries a response from Deuba or his office.

Deuba's camp calls the special convention that elected Thapa illegal, Desh Sanchar reported. It has filed its own schedule for a rival convention on December 7 to 9 with the Election Commission, Lokaantar reported on September 30.

## What the coverage missed

None of the reports this article draws on carries Deuba's own account of the missed invitation, leaving a named public figure's intentions described only through his rival faction's telling.

Reports describing "10,000 delegates and well-wishers" booked into hotels do not say how many are credentialed voting delegates eligible to take part in Monday's nominations, as opposed to supporters along for the event.

## What we still do not know

The Election Commission recognized the Thapa-led central committee in January, and the Supreme Court upheld that in April, the Kathmandu Post reported. A review petition from Deuba's side is pending, the Post reported. Whether that review changes the recognition is open.

Whether Deuba deliberately avoided the invitation or was genuinely unreachable is unresolved. Only Deuba or his private secretary Bhanu Deuba can settle it.

Who is paying to house and move roughly 10,000 people through the convention has not been disclosed. The organizing committee's finance arm would know.

nepali.headline: कांग्रेसको महाधिवेशन सुरु, देउबाको निम्तो सुरक्षागार्डलाई थमाइयो
nepali.dek: सोमबार उम्मेदवारी दर्ता हुँदै छ, तर प्रतिद्वन्द्वी पक्षले देउबालाई उनकै निम्तो हातमा दिन सकेन।
nepali.take: नेपाली कांग्रेसले १५औं महाधिवेशन सुरु गर्दा कुनै बेला पार्टी चलाएका नेताले नै बहिष्कारको आह्वान गरेका छन्। पूर्वप्रधानमन्त्री तथा पूर्वसभापति शेरबहादुर देउबाले यो बहिष्कारको आह्वान गरेका छन्, देश सञ्चारले जनाएको छ। उनकै निम्तो पनि उनीसम्म नपुगेको सहमहासचिव योगेन्द्र चौधरीले अनलाइनखबरलाई बताएका छन्। यो लेखले आधार लिएका कुनै पनि समाचारमा देउबा पक्षको भनाइ नभएकाले ती समाचारमा यो एकतर्फी विवरणलाई कसैले चुनौती दिएको छैन। करिब १० हजार प्रतिनिधि र शुभेच्छुकका लागि भएको होटल बुकिङले पार्टीले ठूलो आयोजना गर्न सक्ने देखाउँछ। तर त्यसले सोमबारको उम्मेदवारी प्रक्रियामा वास्तवमा को को भाग लिन्छन्, वा सर्वोच्च अदालतमा विचाराधीन पुनरावलोकनले निर्वाचन आयोगले जनवरीमा पार्टी सभापति गगन थापाको समितिलाई दिएको मान्यता बदल्छ कि बदल्दैन भन्ने देखाउँदैन।
nepali.body_markdown:
काठमाडौं । नेपाल प्रेसका अनुसार नेपाली कांग्रेसले आइतबार (४ अक्टोबर) दिउँसो २ बजे टुँडिखेल खुला मञ्चबाट १५औं महाधिवेशनको उद्घाटन गरेको पार्टी प्रवक्ता देवराज चालिसेले जनाएका छन्। नेपाली कांग्रेस नेपालको सबैभन्दा पुरानो प्रजातान्त्रिक पार्टी हो। सोमबार (५ अक्टोबर) उम्मेदवारी दर्ता हुने र मंगलबार (६ अक्टोबर)सम्म समापन सत्र र बाँकी कार्यक्रमहरू चलिरहने अनलाइनखबरले जनाएको छ।

यस हप्ता शीर्ष पद जित्नेहरूले नै पार्टीको तर्फबाट बोल्नेछन्। टुँडिखेलमा जम्मा भएका प्रतिनिधिहरूले सोमबारदेखि यिनै उम्मेदवार छनोट गर्न थाल्नेछन्, इकान्तिपुर र नेपालन्युज डटकमले जनाएका छन्।

खबरहब र नेपालन्युज डटकमका अनुसार आयोजक समितिले काठमाडौंभरि करिब १० हजार प्रतिनिधि र शुभेच्छुकलाई राख्न होटल कोठा बुक गरेको छ। नेपाल प्रेसका अनुसार कार्यक्रमस्थल वरिपरि सहभागी र प्रतिनिधि ल्याउने सवारीसाधन राख्न ८ ठाउँमा पार्किङ बनाइएको छ। इकान्तिपुरका अनुसार ३० स्वास्थ्यकर्मी र २ एम्बुलेन्स तयारी अवस्थामा छन्। होटलहरूमा पनि स्वास्थ्य परीक्षण गरिएको इकान्तिपुरले उल्लेख गरेको छ।

## नपुगेको निम्तो

पूर्वप्रधानमन्त्री तथा नेपाली कांग्रेसका पूर्वसभापति शेरबहादुर देउबाले महाधिवेशन बहिष्कार गर्न आग्रह गरेका छन्, देश सञ्चारले जनाएको छ। आफ्नो प्रतिद्वन्द्वी तथा हालका पार्टी सभापति गगन थापाले नेतृत्व गरिरहेको यो महाधिवेशनमा सहभागी हुन देउबाले अस्वीकार गरेका छन्, काठमाडौं पोस्टले जनाएको छ। सभापति थापाले सहमहासचिव योगेन्द्र चौधरीलाई देउबाको निवासमा पठाएर उनलाई प्रमुख अतिथिका रूपमा सहभागी हुन अनुरोध गर्ने निम्तो हातहातै पुर्‍याउन लगाएका थिए, अनलाइनखबर र नेपाल प्रेसले जनाएका छन्।

तर प्रतिनिधिमण्डल देउबासम्मै पुग्न नसकेको चौधरीले बताएका छन्।

"हामी उहाँलाई भेट्न सकेनौं, घरभित्रै पसेका थियौं। भानुजीलाई फोन गर्दा उहाँलाई पनि भेटिएन। त्यसपछि घरमा गएर सुरक्षागार्डलाई दिएर फर्कियौं," चौधरीले अनलाइनखबरसँग भने। चौधरीले यहाँ "भानुजी" भनेर देउबाका निजी सचिव भानु देउबालाई जनाएका हुन्।

अनलाइनखबर र नेपाल प्रेस दुवैमा देउबा वा उनको कार्यालयको प्रतिक्रिया छैन।

देउबा पक्षले थापालाई निर्वाचित गराएको विशेष महाधिवेशनलाई गैरकानुनी भन्दै आएको छ, देश सञ्चारले जनाएको छ। उनीहरूले आगामी ७ देखि ९ डिसेम्बरसम्म हुने आफ्नै समानान्तर महाधिवेशनको तालिका निर्वाचन आयोगमा दर्ता गराएका छन्, लोकान्तरले ३० सेप्टेम्बरमा जनाएको थियो।

## समाचारले छुटाएको कुरा

यो लेखले आधार लिएका कुनै पनि समाचारमा निम्तो नपुगेबारे देउबा आफैंको भनाइ छैन। त्यसैले ती समाचारमा एक सार्वजनिक व्यक्तिको मनसाय उनका प्रतिद्वन्द्वी पक्षको भनाइमार्फत मात्र आएको छ।

होटलमा बुक गरिएका "१० हजार प्रतिनिधि र शुभेच्छुक" को विवरण दिने समाचारहरूले तीमध्ये सोमबारको उम्मेदवारी प्रक्रियामा भाग लिन पाउने मतदाता प्रतिनिधि कति हुन् भनेर खुलाएका छैनन्। कार्यक्रममा साथ आएका समर्थक मात्र कति हुन् भन्ने पनि ती समाचारमा छैन।

## अझै थाहा नभएका कुरा

काठमाडौं पोस्टका अनुसार निर्वाचन आयोगले जनवरीमा थापा नेतृत्वको केन्द्रीय समितिलाई मान्यता दिएको थियो र सर्वोच्च अदालतले अप्रिलमा त्यसलाई सदर गरेको थियो। देउबा पक्षको पुनरावलोकन निवेदन अझै विचाराधीन रहेको पोस्टले थपेको छ। त्यो पुनरावलोकनले उक्त मान्यतामा केही फेरबदल ल्याउने हो वा होइन भन्ने प्रश्न अझै खुला छ।

देउबाले जानाजानी निम्तो टारेका हुन् वा साँच्चै भेट्न नसकिने अवस्थामा थिए भन्ने प्रश्न अझै अनुत्तरित छ। यो कुरा देउबा वा उनका निजी सचिव भानु देउबाले मात्र प्रस्ट पार्न सक्छन्।

करिब १० हजार मानिसलाई बास र ओहोरदोहोर गराउने खर्च कसले बेहोर्दै छ भन्ने सार्वजनिक भएको छैन। आयोजक समितिको आर्थिक पक्ष हेर्नेहरूलाई यो थाहा हुनुपर्छ।

fact_problems: The sentence puts the convention's opening under Chaudhary's attribution, when the record sources it to spokesperson Chalise via Nepal Press. It also joins two facts the English keeps apart, and भने…भइसकेको implies a timing link the record does not carry.

The record limits this to the reports the article draws on: in them, Deuba's intentions are described only through the rival faction. 'मात्र सार्वजनिक भएको छ' widens it to everything made public anywhere.

language_fixes.fix: यस हप्ता शीर्ष पद जित्नेहरूले नै नेपाली कांग्रेसको तर्फबाट बोल्नेछन्। तर पूर्वसभापति शेरबहादुर देउबाले महाधिवेशन बहिष्कारको आह्वान गरेको देश सञ्चारले जनाएको छ।

angles.claim: Sher Bahadur Deuba's camp was not freshly 'boycotting' a new decision today — Deuba had already called the Thapa-led process an outcome of an 'illegal special convention' and his faction had already filed a rival Dec 7-9 convention timetable with the Election Commission weeks before Sunday's Tundikhel opening.
angles.why_it_matters: Framing the boycott as the day's news obscures that the institutional rupture — two rival conventions, one filed with the state's election body — was settled policy on Deuba's side since mid/late September; readers need to know this is the scheduled playing-out of an old fracture, not a new one, before judging who is escalating.

evidence.fact: Reports the Thapa-led convention scheduled Oct 2-5 against Deuba faction's parallel convention set for Dec 7-9, and that roughly 30 leaders had shifted away from Deuba, as of September 16.
Deuba is reported calling the Thapa-led convention the outcome of an 'illegal special convention' and urging supporters to boycott it.
Reports that Deuba's group submitted its own parallel convention timetable to the Election Commission on September 30.

angles.claim: The only account in today's coverage of NC leaders failing to deliver the chief-guest invitation to Deuba rests on a single on-record quote from one party official, co-general secretary Yogendra Chaudhary; no outlet in today's set carries a response, confirmation, or denial from Deuba or his secretariat.
angles.why_it_matters: Deuba is a named public figure whose intentions are being characterized through his rival faction's own telling of events; without his side, readers cannot know whether he was genuinely unreachable or deliberately avoided the overture, and the story risks amplifying one camp's narrative as settled fact.

evidence.fact: Quotes Yogendra Chaudhary saying the team went to Deuba's residence, could not reach him by phone through his private secretary Bhanu Deuba, and left the invitation with security staff at the house.
Reports that co-general secretary Chaudhary, sent by president Thapa, could not meet Deuba in person even after going to his residence.

angles.claim: The widely repeated figure of 'roughly 10,000 delegates and well-wishers' with hotel bookings, eight parking sites and 30 health workers/two ambulances conflates credentialed voting delegates with spectators and supporters, and no outlet in today's set breaks out how many of the 10,000 actually hold voting rights at Monday's candidate nominations.
angles.why_it_matters: The outcome that matters politically — who gets nominated and who controls the party — is decided by credentialed delegates, not by the total headcount in hotels; an undifferentiated 'crowd size' figure can be used by either faction to claim a stronger mandate than the voting math supports.

evidence.fact: Reports Congress has arranged accommodation for 10,000 delegates and well-wishers, without separating the two categories.
Reports eight parking sites were arranged for 'participants and representatives' coming to the convention venue, again without a delegate-only count.

angles.claim: Deuba's camp has already formalized the split by filing a separate Dec 7-9 convention schedule with the Election Commission, but no outlet covering today's Tundikhel opening addresses whether or when the Commission will decide which of the two rival conventions — and therefore which faction — is recognized as the legitimate Nepali Congress leadership.
angles.why_it_matters: Election Commission recognition determines which faction can use the Nepali Congress name and election symbol in future polls — a question with direct consequences for Nepal's coalition politics that none of today's logistics-focused reporting touches.

evidence.fact: Confirms Deuba's group submitted its own parallel convention timetable to the Election Commission.
Confirms two competing convention schedules exist — Thapa-led Oct 2-5 and Deuba faction's Dec 7-9.

unanswered.question: Will the Election Commission formally recognize the Tundikhel convention or Deuba's filed Dec 7-9 schedule as the legitimate Nepali Congress general convention, and on what legal basis under the Political Parties Act?

unanswered.question: How many of the roughly 10,000 people housed and transported for the convention are credentialed voting delegates eligible to take part in Monday's candidate nominations, as opposed to well-wishers and supporters?

unanswered.question: Did Sher Bahadur Deuba decline the chief-guest invitation deliberately, or was he genuinely unreachable as co-general secretary Chaudhary described, and does Deuba's office dispute that account?
unanswered.who_could_answer: Sher Bahadur Deuba or his private secretariat (private secretary Bhanu Deuba)

unanswered.question: Who is funding the hotel bookings for roughly 10,000 people, the eight parking-site arrangements and the health standby team, and what is the total cost of staging the convention?
unanswered.who_could_answer: Nepali Congress party treasurer/finance department or the Convention Organizing Committee's logistics/finance sub-committee

unanswered.question: Beyond the roughly 30 leaders reported in mid-September as having shifted away from Deuba, how many additional named senior NC leaders have since confirmed attendance at Tundikhel, and has that number changed since the parallel Dec 7-9 schedule was filed?

investigation.summary: Today's wall of near-identical logistics stories (parking, hotels, ambulances) obscures that the real news — Deuba's boycott and his camp's rival Dec 7-9 convention filing with the Election Commission — was already locked in place three weeks ago, and that the one fresh detail, the failed hand-delivered invitation to Deuba, rests entirely on one party official's account with no response sought from Deuba's side. No outlet asks who will adjudicate which of the two rival conventions the Election Commission will recognize, or how many of the reported 10,000 attendees are actually voting delegates — both of which matter more to the outcome than who holds a parking permit.

Ekantipur, Nepalnews, OnlineKhabar and Nepal Press support it, but the invitation account must be attributed to co-general secretary Yogendra Chaudhary, note that no Deuba response appears, and keep 'illegal' as Deuba's claim. Weakest dimension is personal stakes.

findings.passage: Nepali Congress opens 15th convention at Tundikhel as Deuba invitation goes undelivered
findings.problem: The invitation was delivered to Deuba's residence and handed to his security guard, per co-general secretary Chaudhary's own account in OnlineKhabar and Nepal Press. 'Goes undelivered' is not what happened, only face-to-face delivery to Deuba himself failed. The headline overstates the record and will be the only thing most readers see.
findings.suggested_fix: Change to something like 'Nepali Congress opens 15th convention at Tundikhel as Deuba invitation never reaches him' or 'as Deuba stays unreachable', matching the body's own accurate framing.

findings.passage: Whether the Election Commission will recognize Thapa's convention or Deuba's filed December schedule is unanswered. Only the Commission or Nepali Congress's own statute committee could say.
findings.problem: This is presented in the newsroom's own investigative addition as a fully open question, but the record shows the Election Commission already recognized the Thapa-led Central Working Committee in January 2026, and the Supreme Court upheld that recognition in April 2026. A review petition by Deuba is pending, but that is a narrower, already-partly-settled question than the binary the article poses. The same overstatement repeats in the caption ('Which of two rival conventions the Election Commission recognizes is still unsettled') and in the take ('which convention Nepal's Election Commission will ultimately recognize as real').
findings.suggested_fix: Correct all three instances to state that the Election Commission already recognizes the Thapa-led committee and the Supreme Court upheld that in April, and that what remains open is narrower: whether the pending Supreme Court review changes that recognition, and whether the EC treats this week's convention as completing that mandate before the mid-December statutory deadline.

findings.passage: The party booked hotels for roughly 10,000 delegates and well-wishers and arranged eight parking sites and two ambulances on standby, Nepal Press and ekantipur reported.
findings.problem: This caption sentence misattributes the hotel-booking figure. The article's own body and sources list credit the 10,000 figure to Khabarhub and Nepalnews.com, not Nepal Press or ekantipur. Nepal Press is the source for the parking detail and ekantipur for the ambulance detail. Bundling three different outlets' facts under a wrong shared attribution breaks the rule that attribution is part of the fact.
findings.suggested_fix: Split or correct attribution: 'The party booked hotels for roughly 10,000 delegates and well-wishers, Khabarhub and Nepalnews.com reported. It arranged eight parking sites, Nepal Press reported, and two ambulances on standby, ekantipur reported.'

findings.passage: Nepali Congress has anchored or propped up nearly every ruling coalition in Nepal for three decades.
findings.problem: This sweeping historical claim carries no named source and does not appear in the sources list, violating the rule that every fact or claim traces to a named source. It reads as the newsroom's own unsupported generalization.
findings.suggested_fix: Either attribute the claim to a specific outlet or analysis that states it, or cut it and replace with a narrower, sourced fact about NC's current seat count or coalition role.

findings.passage: Deuba's camp has called Thapa's convention illegal and filed its own schedule for a rival convention on December 7 to 9 with the Election Commission, Desh Sanchar and Lokaantar reported in September.
findings.problem: Desh Sanchar's report quotes Deuba calling the convention 'an outcome of an illegal special convention,' meaning he branded the earlier January special convention (which elected Thapa) illegal, not the October 4 to 6 convention itself. Collapsing this into 'called Thapa's convention illegal' blurs which event Deuba is actually disputing.
findings.suggested_fix: Specify: 'Deuba's camp has called the special convention that elected Thapa illegal and, on that basis, is boycotting this convention and has filed its own December 7 to 9 schedule with the Election Commission.'

findings.passage: The party booked hotels for roughly 10,000 delegates and well-wishers and arranged eight parking sites and two ambulances on standby, Nepal Press and ekantipur reported.
findings.problem: This caption sentence runs about 25 words and packs three different numbers (10,000, eight, two) into one sentence, against the house style rule of most sentences under twelve words, none over twenty, and one number per sentence.
findings.suggested_fix: Break into two short sentences, each carrying one number, e.g. 'The party booked hotels for roughly 10,000 delegates and well-wishers, Khabarhub reported. It also set up eight parking sites and put two ambulances on standby.'

findings.passage: Nepali Congress opens 15th convention at Tundikhel as Deuba invitation goes undelivered
findings.problem: Because the invitation was in fact physically delivered to Deuba's residence, framing it as 'undelivered' could be read as implying the NC organizing side failed at a basic task, when the record shows the failure was specifically in reaching Deuba in person. This slightly misrepresents the logistics in a way that is unfair to the delivering team without being a defamation risk.
findings.suggested_fix: Use precise language throughout: the invitation reached the residence and the security guard, not Deuba himself.

red_team.summary: The body is mostly well sourced and attributes contested claims properly, but the headline's 'invitation goes undelivered' overstates what happened since the invitation did reach Deuba's residence and guard. The newsroom's own investigative addition and the caption and take repeat a significant omission by treating Election Commission recognition of the rival conventions as a fully open question when the Commission already recognized the Thapa-led committee and the Supreme Court upheld that in April 2026. The caption also misattributes the hotel-booking figure to the wrong outlets and crams three numbers into one overlong sentence, and one sweeping unsourced claim about NC's three-decade coalition role needs either a source or a cut.

responses.response: The red team is right. Chaudhary's own account says the guard took the invitation at the residence, that is delivery to the house, just not a face to face handoff. "Goes undelivered" misstates that and will mislead readers who never read past the headline.
responses.proposed_edit: Change headline to: "Nepali Congress opens 15th convention at Tundikhel as Deuba invitation never reaches him"

responses.response: The article's framing as a clean open binary is thin, but the red team's suggested fix overstates how settled this is too. Public record shows the Election Commission recognized the Thapa led committee in January, the Supreme Court upheld that in April, but the Supreme Court then reopened its own review of that ruling in August 2026, which is why the question is live again heading into this week's convention. The article should have carried that chronology instead of treating it as a fact free unknown, but it should not swing to calling the matter settled either.
responses.proposed_edit: Revise the paragraph to: "The Election Commission recognized Thapa's central committee in January, and the Supreme Court upheld that in April. In August, the court reopened its own review of that ruling, so which convention the Commission ultimately treats as valid is open again. Only the Commission or the court can settle it." Apply the same correction to the matching lines in the caption and the take.

responses.proposed_edit: Rewrite as: "The party booked hotels for roughly 10,000 delegates and well-wishers, Khabarhub and Nepalnews.com reported. It set up eight parking sites, Nepal Press reported, and kept two ambulances on standby, ekantipur reported."

responses.response: Correct catch. No outlet in the sources list is cited for this three decade coalition claim, so it reads as the newsroom's own unsupported generalization, which the accuracy rules forbid.
responses.proposed_edit: Cut the sentence, or replace with a sourced fact, e.g. "Nepali Congress is Nepal's largest party by seats in the current Parliament, according to [named outlet with election data if available]." If no clean sourced replacement exists, cut it and move directly to the next sentence about who speaks for the party in coalition bargaining.

responses.response: Same underlying problem as f1, applied to the defensibility of the framing toward the NC organizing team specifically. Fixing the headline language to reflect that the invitation reached the residence and the guard, not Deuba in person, resolves both the accuracy and the fairness concern in one move.
responses.proposed_edit: Covered by the f1 headline fix. No separate change needed once the headline reads "as Deuba invitation never reaches him" instead of "goes undelivered."

defense.summary: Most findings hold up. The headline and the duplicate fairness point both trace to the same loose word, undelivered, when the record shows the invitation reached the house and the guard, just not Deuba himself, so both get the same fix. The caption has a real attribution error, bundling three outlets' separate facts under the wrong shared credit, and a related style violation for stacking three numbers in one sentence, both fixed together. The unsourced three decade coalition claim should be cut or sourced. The Desh Sanchar quote shows Deuba was calling the January special convention illegal, not Sunday's event, so that sentence needs tightening. The one finding that needed real pushback was f2: public record shows the Election Commission and Supreme Court did rule on this in January and April, but the Supreme Court reopened its own review in August, so the question is genuinely live again, not settled the way the red team's fix implies. The article should add that chronology rather than accept the red team's framing wholesale. The card headline's word count is short of style and gets expanded.

rulings.note: Chaudhary told OnlineKhabar and Nepal Press the invitation was left with Deuba's security guard at the residence. 'Goes undelivered' misstates that. The defence's 'never reaches him' still states the delivering side's account as fact, so the headline should state only the proven action.

The binary framing ignores the January EC recognition and the April Supreme Court ruling the red team cites from the Kathmandu Post of September 27. The defence's claim that the court reopened its review in August has no URL or named outlet and cannot be adopted. Use only what the Post piece carries.
The caption credits the 10,000 hotel figure to Nepal Press and ekantipur. The body and sources list credit Khabarhub and Nepalnews.com.
The three decade coalition claim has no source in the list. Cut it.
The Desh Sanchar wording targets the special convention that elected Thapa. The sentence must name that event.
The caption sentence carries three numbers and about 25 words, against the one number and twenty word rules. Several other caption sentences also run past twenty words.
